summary: BCSS native 22-class annotation and repository 22-to-unified remap contract, including protected collapsed-zero provenance and retained tumor subtypes.

annotation_traits: region annotations were harmonized from multiple pathologists
native classes are substantially finer than the unified ontology
multiple biologically distinct native classes collapse into Stroma, Tumor, Blood vessel, Other tissue, or zero
semantic_limitations: Unified zero combines outside-ROI, excluded, and undetermined pixels; it is not a biological tissue class.
Unified Stroma also contains native glandular secretions in this repository remap.
Unified Other tissue mixes blood, metaplasia, fat, mucoid material, nerve, skin adnexa, and native other.

rules.claim: Preserve every unified-zero pixel because the remap cannot distinguish outside-ROI, excluded, and undetermined provenance after collapse.
rules.required_observation: Compare source and candidate masks at all zero pixels and verify no zero component is used as an edit anchor.
counterexamples: Growing tumor into an excluded strip.
Filling an undetermined hole with stroma because it appears internal.
expected_morphology: The candidate retains the exact source zero footprint.
forbidden_morphology: Zero-label filling, erosion, seeding, or bridging.
known_limitations: Native zero provenance is unavailable once only the remapped mask is retained.

rules.claim: Do not reverse-infer a unique native tissue from a many-to-one unified label.
rules.required_observation: Use the original label map when available; otherwise keep the canonical label coarse and ask the critic only for visual plausibility.
exceptions: A separately retained native mask digest and pixel-aligned native mask may restore the native identity.
counterexamples: Calling every Stroma pixel fibrous stroma even though glandular secretion was mapped there.
Calling every Blood vessel pixel a blood vessel even though native lymphatics share the canonical label.
expected_morphology: Candidate selection is compatible with H&E and the canonical label without inventing a native subtype.
forbidden_morphology: Tool choice that requires a tissue subtype absent from the retained mask.
known_limitations: Repository remap behavior must be validated against the exact preprocessing revision.

rules.claim: A burden-only edit must not silently convert invasive tumor, DCIS, and angioinvasion fine labels into one another.
rules.required_observation: Audit changed fine IDs against the primitive source/target transition and preserve unrequested tumor subtypes pixel-exactly.
exceptions: A dedicated reviewed DCIS-invasion or vascular-invasion primitive.
counterexamples: Expanding generic tumor by overwriting a DCIS duct.
Relabeling angioinvasion as ordinary invasive tumor to simplify the boundary.
expected_morphology: Unrequested fine tumor classes retain their identity and geometry.
known_limitations: Fine-label accuracy depends on preserving the repository's fine remap rather than only a coarse mask.

rules.claim: Do not erase or absorb small labeled regions merely because their area is below a generic morphology threshold.
rules.required_observation: Preserve every unrequested label exactly and compare component topology before and after the edit.
counterexamples: Morphological closing that removes a tiny vessel or normal duct.
Smoothing a tumor boundary by swallowing a small immune component.
forbidden_morphology: Generic denoising of legitimate minority labels.
known_limitations: Rare-class size envelopes require complete-training-set statistics.

rules.claim: Require the exact preprocessing revision and original label-map digest; do not infer BCSS semantics from breast organ metadata.
rules.required_observation: Verify declared annotation profile and mapping provenance before loading rules.
counterexamples: Treating any breast segmentation as BCSS.
Mixing a 22-class native mask with an eight-class profile declaration.
known_limitations: No full immutable BCSS evidence manifest is mounted in this repository yet.
